_readme: THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Edit the text and videoUrl fields, then redeploy. Every videoUrl that still starts with REPLACE_ME will fall back to the idle video. See README.md, section 'Step 6: Upload your videos'.

meta.introLine: Type me a message and I'll answer. Yes, it's really me. Sort of.

categories.label: Greeting
categories.description: A simple hello or opening message

variants.text: Hey! You came. That's more than I expected.
Welcome to my very professional farewell website.
Oh. Hi. I was just standing here looping.

categories.label: Goodbye
categories.description: Saying bye, farewell, or signing off

variants.text: Bye! Or as I'm now contractually required to say — let's keep in touch.
See you around. Genuinely.

categories.label: Compliment
categories.description: Praising me, saying I was good at my job or a good colleague
triggers: you were so good at your job

variants.text: Stop it. Keep going. Stop it.
I'm putting that in writing and forwarding it to HR on my way out.
Honestly? Same to you.

categories.label: Playful roast
categories.description: Teasing, insulting, or roasting me in a friendly way

variants.text: Wow. On my last week. Bold.
You know I've still got building access until Friday, right?
Fair. Genuinely fair.

categories.label: Why are you leaving
categories.description: Asking my reason for leaving the job

variants.text: New chapter, same me, slightly better chair.
It was time. Also nobody ever fixed that printer.

categories.label: Where are you going
categories.description: Asking about my new job, new company, or next destination
triggers: are you going to a competitor

variants.text: Somewhere new. Somewhere exciting. Somewhere with a working coffee machine.
Buy me a drink and I'll tell you everything.

categories.label: Keep in touch
categories.description: Asking to stay in contact, swap numbers, or connect online

variants.text: Absolutely. LinkedIn, WhatsApp, carrier pigeon. I'm reachable.
Please do. I'll be the one replying six days later.

categories.label: We'll miss you
categories.description: Telling me they'll miss me or that it won't be the same without me
triggers: the team won't be the same
who am i going to talk to now

variants.text: Don't. I'm barely holding it together as it is.
I'll miss you too. Obviously.

categories.label: Good luck
categories.description: Wishing me luck or success in whatever comes next

variants.text: Thank you. I'll need roughly all of it.
That means more than you know.

categories.label: Thank you
categories.description: Thanking me for help, work, mentoring, or friendship

variants.text: No — thank you. Sincerely.
That means a lot. Now stop, people are looking.

categories.label: Work in-jokes
categories.description: References to meetings, standups, Slack, tickets, emails, deadlines, office life
triggers: this could have been an email

variants.text: Not my problem after Friday. Say it with me.
I've marked it Won't Fix and I've never been happier.
I'm declining that invite from beyond the grave.

categories.label: Any advice
categories.description: Asking me for advice, wisdom, or tips for the people staying behind
triggers: what would you tell your younger self

variants.text: Take the lunch break. Every single day. That's it. That's the wisdom.
Ask the stupid question early. It's much cheaper than asking it late.

categories.label: Favourite memory
categories.description: Asking about my best memory, favourite moment, or highlight here

variants.text: Too many to pick. Most of them happened in a kitchen, not a meeting room.
You know the one. We agreed never to speak of it.

categories.label: Food, coffee and snacks
categories.description: Anything about lunch, coffee, snacks, the office kitchen or the fridge

variants.text: The fridge is yours now. I'm so sorry.
I'm taking the good mug. This isn't a discussion.

categories.label: Will you come back
categories.description: Asking whether I'll return, visit, or regret leaving

variants.text: Never say never. Especially if you're buying lunch.
I'll visit. I'll even sign in at reception like a stranger.

categories.label: What will you miss
categories.description: Asking what I will miss about this place or these people
triggers: what are you going to miss

variants.text: The people. Obviously the people. Absolutely not the parking.
All of you. Some of you slightly more. You know who you are.

categories.label: Leaving drinks and celebration
categories.description: Talk of the send-off, leaving drinks, party, cheers, celebration

variants.text: First round's on me. Second round's on you. Third round is a mystery.
I'll be there. I'll be emotional. Bring tissues.

categories.label: Affectionate or soppy
categories.description: Warm, soppy, or affectionate messages, hugs, work-spouse jokes

variants.text: Love you too. In an entirely HR-compliant way.
That's very sweet and I'm choosing to believe you mean it.

categories.label: Nonsense and chaos
categories.description: Gibberish, keyboard mashing, laughing, random silly noise, emoji spam

variants.text: I have no idea what that meant and I respect it enormously.
Understood. Completely. No notes.

categories.label: Anything else
categories.description: Use this when the message does not fit any other category

variants.text: I have no idea how to respond to that, and I love that for us.
Interesting. Say more. Actually, don't — I'm leaving.
That one's going in the memoir.
